steps.title: Create religiosity scale
steps.description: Construct the religiosity latent variable from the 9-item scale.

options.label: Mean of religiosity items
options.rationale: Simple average is interpretable, preserves metric, and is standard for summative scales with homogeneous items.
options.spec: Compute relig = (rel_1 + rel_2 + rel_3 + rel_4 + rel_5 + rel_6 + rel_7 + rel_8 + rel_9) / 9; add column 'relig' to dataframe; return dataframe.

options.label: PCA first component
options.rationale: PCA extracts the dominant latent dimension, potentially improving reliability if items weigh differently on the construct.
options.spec: Standardise the 9 rel_* items to z-scores; compute first principal component; orient so that loading on rel_1 is positive; add column 'relig' to dataframe; return dataframe.

steps.title: Create cultural norms scale
steps.description: Construct the perceived cultural norms variable from the 2-item scale.

options.label: Mean of cultural norms items
options.rationale: With only two items, the mean is equivalent to sum and is the most transparent and stable approach.
options.spec: Compute cnorm = (cnorm_1 + cnorm_2) / 2; add column 'cnorm' to dataframe; return dataframe.

options.label: PCA first component
options.rationale: PCA may better capture shared variance if items differ in precision, though with two items it is proportional to the mean.
options.spec: Standardise cnorm_1 and cnorm_2 to z-scores; compute first principal component; orient so that loading on cnorm_1 is positive; add column 'cnorm' to dataframe; return dataframe.

steps.description: Choose which well-being composite to use as the outcome.

options.label: Overall well-being mean
options.rationale: The wb_overall_mean is the validated 18-item composite and the primary outcome of interest in well-being research.
options.spec: Use wb_overall_mean as the outcome; write ctx['outcome'] = 'wb_overall_mean'; return dataframe unchanged.

options.label: Psychological well-being mean
options.rationale: Psychological well-being may be more proximate to religiosity than physical or social domains, offering a focused test.
options.spec: Use wb_psych_mean as the outcome; write ctx['outcome'] = 'wb_psych_mean'; return dataframe unchanged.

options.label: Social well-being mean
options.rationale: Religiosity often operates through social mechanisms; social well-being may capture relational benefits of faith.
options.spec: Use wb_soc_mean as the outcome; write ctx['outcome'] = 'wb_soc_mean'; return dataframe unchanged.

steps.title: Choose covariate adjustment set
steps.description: Select demographic and country-level controls for the model.

options.label: No covariates
options.rationale: Estimates the bivariate interaction; useful as a baseline to assess confounding by added controls.
options.spec: Write ctx['covariates'] = []; return dataframe unchanged.

options.label: Age, gender, education, SES
options.rationale: Standard demographic confounders; age, gender, education and SES are associated with both religiosity and well-being.
options.spec: Write ctx['covariates'] = ['age', 'gender', 'education', 'ses']; return dataframe unchanged.

options.label: Demographics + country GDP
options.rationale: Country-level economic context (gdp_scaled) may confound the religiosity-well-being relation across nations.
options.spec: Write ctx['covariates'] = ['age', 'gender', 'education', 'ses', 'gdp_scaled']; return dataframe unchanged.

steps.title: Estimate interaction model
steps.description: Regress well-being on standardised religiosity, cultural norms, their interaction, and covariates; extract the interaction coefficient.

options.label: OLS with HC3 SEs
options.rationale: OLS is appropriate for continuous outcomes; HC3 standard errors guard against heteroskedasticity without assuming clustering.
options.spec: Standardise relig and cnorm to z-scores (mean 0, sd 1); compute interaction term relig_x_cnorm = relig_z * cnorm_z; if ctx['covariates'] is not empty, standardise those covariates (except gender) to z-scores; fit OLS: ctx['outcome'] ~ relig_z + cnorm_z + relig_x_cnorm + [covariates]; use HC3 robust SEs; extract coefficient, 95% CI, p-value for relig_x_cnorm; return dict with estimate, ci_low, ci_high, p_value.

options.label: OLS clustered by country
options.rationale: Respondents are nested within countries; clustering SEs by country accounts for intra-class correlation and avoids inflated Type I error.
options.spec: Standardise relig and cnorm to z-scores; compute interaction term relig_x_cnorm = relig_z * cnorm_z; if ctx['covariates'] is not empty, standardise those covariates (except gender) to z-scores; fit OLS: ctx['outcome'] ~ relig_z + cnorm_z + relig_x_cnorm + [covariates]; cluster SEs by country; extract coefficient, 95% CI, p-value for relig_x_cnorm; return dict with estimate, ci_low, ci_high, p_value.

data.reason: Clustering standard errors by country is appropriate for nested data and controls for intra-country correlation without altering the estimand.
Using social well-being as outcome is a theoretically justified alternative focusing on relational pathways; it remains a valid well-being dimension without changing the estimand.
Excluding attention-check failures is common practice to improve data quality and reduce noise, though some argue it may introduce bias if failures are non-random.

Using the first PCA component is a reasonable alternative to simple averaging for constructing a latent scale, especially when items may have unequal loadings; it preserves the estimand and is commonly accepted in psychometrics.

Using a theoretically relevant subdomain like psychological well-being as the outcome is a reasonable alternative when justified by proximity to the predictor; it does not change the estimand's structure.
Adding country-level GDP as a covariate is a reasonable extension to control for macroeconomic confounding in cross-national studies of religiosity and well-being.

With exactly two standardized items, the first principal component is a linear rescaling of their mean, preserving the interaction effect up to a constant factor; thus the standardized coefficient remains unchanged.

Omitting key confounders like age, gender, education, and SES risks severe omitted variable bias, especially since these are standard controls in religiosity-well-being research and likely correlate with both predictors and outcome.

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf

def estimate(df, ctx):
    # Standardise religiosity and cultural norms to z-scores
    relig = df['relig']
    cnorm = df['cnorm']
    relig_z = (relig - relig.mean()) / relig.std()
    cnorm_z = (cnorm - cnorm.mean()) / cnorm.std()
    # Interaction term
    interaction = relig_z * cnorm_z
    # Build covariate list from ctx
    covariates = ctx.get('covariates', [])
    # Prepare data: drop rows with missing outcome or predictors
    outcome = ctx['outcome']
    mask = df[outcome].notna() & interaction.notna()
    mask = mask & df['relig'].notna() & df['cnorm'].notna()
    for c in covariates:
        if c in df.columns:
            mask = mask & df[c].notna()
    data = df[mask].copy()
    n = len(data)
    if n == 0:
        return {"estimate": np.nan, "ci_low": np.nan, "ci_high": np.nan, "p_value": np.nan, "n": 0}
    # Standardise outcome and covariates (except gender)
    data[outcome] = (data[outcome] - data[outcome].mean()) / data[outcome].std()
    for c in covariates:
        if c in data.columns and c != 'gender':
            data[c] = (data[c] - data[c].mean()) / data[c].std()
    # Add standardized variables to data
    data['relig_z'] = relig_z.loc[data.index]
    data['cnorm_z'] = cnorm_z.loc[data.index]
    data['interaction'] = interaction.loc[data.index]
    # Construct formula
    terms = ["relig_z", "cnorm_z", "interaction"]
    for c in covariates:
        if c in data.columns:
            terms.append(c)
    formula = outcome + " ~ " + " + ".join(terms)
    # Fit OLS with HC3
    try:
        model = smf.ols(formula=formula, data=data).fit(cov_type="HC3")
        # Extract interaction coefficient
        coeff = model.params['interaction']
        se = model.bse['interaction']
        # 95% CI
        ci_low = coeff - 1.96 * se
        ci_high = coeff + 1.96 * se
        p_value = model.pvalues['interaction']
        # Ensure ci_low < ci_high
        if ci_low > ci_high:
            ci_low, ci_high = ci_high, ci_low
        return {"estimate": float(coeff), "ci_low": float(ci_low), "ci_high": float(ci_high), "p_value": float(p_value), "n": n}

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf

def estimate(df, ctx):
    # Standardise religiosity and cultural norms to z-scores
    relig = df['relig']
    cnorm = df['cnorm']
    relig_z = (relig - relig.mean()) / relig.std()
    cnorm_z = (cnorm - cnorm.mean()) / cnorm.std()
    # Interaction term
    interaction = relig_z * cnorm_z
    # Build covariate list from ctx
    covariates = ctx.get('covariates', [])
    # Prepare data: drop rows with missing outcome or predictors
    outcome = ctx['outcome']
    mask = df[outcome].notna() & interaction.notna()
    mask = mask & df['relig'].notna() & df['cnorm'].notna()
    for c in covariates:
        if c in df.columns:
            mask = mask & df[c].notna()
    data = df[mask].copy()
    n = len(data)
    if n == 0:
        return {"estimate": np.nan, "ci_low": np.nan, "ci_high": np.nan, "p_value": np.nan, "n": 0}
    # Standardise outcome and covariates (except gender)
    data[outcome] = (data[outcome] - data[outcome].mean()) / data[outcome].std()
    for c in covariates:
        if c in data.columns and c != 'gender':
            data[c] = (data[c] - data[c].mean()) / data[c].std()
    # Add standardized variables to data
    data['relig_z'] = relig_z.loc[data.index]
    data['cnorm_z'] = cnorm_z.loc[data.index]
    data['interaction'] = interaction.loc[data.index]
    # Construct formula
    terms = ["relig_z", "cnorm_z", "interaction"]
    for c in covariates:
        if c in data.columns:
            terms.append(c)
    formula = outcome + " ~ " + " + ".join(terms)
    # Fit OLS with HC3
    try:
        model = smf.ols(formula=formula, data=data).fit(cov_type="HC3")
        # Extract interaction coefficient
        coeff = model.params['interaction']
        se = model.bse['interaction']
        # 95% CI
        ci_low = coeff - 1.96 * se
        ci_high = coeff + 1.96 * se
        p_value = model.pvalues['interaction']
        # Ensure ci_low < ci_high
        if ci_low > ci_high:
            ci_low, ci_high = ci_high, ci_low
        return {"estimate": float(coeff), "ci_low": float(ci_low), "ci_high": float(ci_high), "p_value": float(p_value), "n": n}
    except Exception:
        return {"estimate": np.nan, "ci_low": np.nan, "ci_high": np.nan, "p_value": np.nan, "n": n}

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf

def estimate(df, ctx):
    # Standardise religiosity and cultural norms to z-scores
    relig = df['relig']
    cnorm = df['cnorm']
    relig_z = (relig - relig.mean()) / relig.std()
    cnorm_z = (cnorm - cnorm.mean()) / cnorm.std()
    # Interaction term
    interaction = relig_z * cnorm_z
    # Build covariate list from ctx
    covariates = ctx.get('covariates', [])
    # Prepare data: drop rows with missing outcome or predictors
    outcome = ctx['outcome']
    mask = df[outcome].notna() & interaction.notna()
    mask = mask & df['relig'].notna() & df['cnorm'].notna()
    for c in covariates:
        if c in df.columns:
            mask = mask & df[c].notna()
    data = df[mask].copy()
    n = len(data)
    if n == 0:
        return {"estimate": np.nan, "ci_low": np.nan, "ci_high": np.nan, "p_value": np.nan, "n": 0}
    # Standardise outcome and covariates (except gender)
    data[outcome] = (data[outcome] - data[outcome].mean()) / data[outcome].std()
    for c in covariates:
        if c in data.columns and c != 'gender':
            data[c] = (data[c] - data[c].mean()) / data[c].std()
    # Add standardized variables to data
    data['relig_z'] = relig_z.loc[data.index]
    data['cnorm_z'] = cnorm_z.loc[data.index]
    data['interaction'] = interaction.loc[data.index]
    # Construct formula
    terms = ["relig_z", "cnorm_z", "interaction"]
    for c in covariates:
        if c in data.columns:
            terms.append(c)
    formula = outcome + " ~ " + " + ".join(terms)
    # Fit OLS with HC3
    try:
        model = smf.ols(formula=formula, data=data).fit(cov_type="HC3")
        # Extract interaction coefficient
        coeff = model.params['interaction']
        se = model.bse['interaction']
        # 95% CI
        ci_low = coeff - 1.96 * se
        ci_high = coeff + 1.96 * se
        p_value = model.pvalues['interaction']
        # Ensure ci_low < ci_high
        if ci_low > ci_high:
            ci_low, ci_high = ci_high, ci_low
        return {"estimate": float(coeff), "ci_low": float(ci_low), "ci_high": float(ci_high), "p_value": float(p_value), "n": n}
    except Exception:
        return {"estimate": np.nan, "ci_low": np.nan, "ci_high": np.nan, "p_value": np.nan, "n": n}

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm


def estimate(df, ctx):
    outcome_column = str(ctx.get('outcome', 'wb_overall_mean'))
    names = [] + [str(c) for c in ctx.get('covariates', [])]
    names = [c for c in dict.fromkeys(names) if c not in [outcome_column, 'relig', 'cnorm']]
    used = list(dict.fromkeys([outcome_column, 'relig', 'cnorm', 'country'] + names))
    data = df.dropna(subset=used)
    finite = [c for c in used if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(data[c])]
    data = data[np.isfinite(data[finite].astype(float)).all(axis=1)]
    if len(data) and data['relig'].nunique() < 2:
        raise ValueError('the exposure ' + 'relig' + ' has the same value in every row, so it is collinear with the intercept and its effect cannot be estimated: the earlier step that builds it produced a constant. A threshold taken from a numpy median, percentile or quantile is NaN when the column has missing values, and no row then passes it. The pandas median and quantile methods skip missing values')
    scaled = ['relig', 'cnorm', outcome_column]
    data = data.assign(**{c: (data[c].astype(float) - data[c].astype(float).mean()) / (data[c].astype(float).std() or 1.0) for c in scaled})
    core = data[['relig', 'cnorm']].astype(float).assign(exposure_by_moderator=data['relig'].astype(float) * data['cnorm'].astype(float))
    parts = [core]
    numeric = [c for c in names if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(data[c])]
    other = [c for c in names if c not in numeric]
    if numeric:
        parts.append(data[numeric].astype(float))
    if other:
        dummies = pd.get_dummies(data[other].astype(str), drop_first=True, dtype=float)
        parts.append(dummies)
    exog = sm.add_constant(pd.concat(parts, axis=1), has_constant='add')
    labels = pd.Series(exog.columns.map(str))
    repeats = labels.groupby(labels).cumcount()
    exog.columns = [f'{c}_repeat{n}' if n else c for c, n in zip(labels, repeats)]
    protected = ['const', *map(str, core.columns)]
    basis = np.zeros((len(exog), 0))
    aliased = []
    for column in list(exog.columns):
        vector = exog[column].to_numpy(dtype=float)
        size = float(np.linalg.norm(vector))
        residual = vector / size if size else vector
        for _ in range(2):
            residual = residual - basis @ (basis.T @ residual)
        size = float(np.linalg.norm(residual))
        if size >= 1e-07:
            basis = np.column_stack([basis, residual / size])
        elif str(column) not in protected:
            aliased.append(str(column))
    kept = [c for c in exog.columns if c not in aliased]
    tangled = []
    for column in aliased:
        target = exog[column].to_numpy(dtype=float)
        weights = np.linalg.lstsq(exog[kept].to_numpy(dtype=float), target, rcond=None)[0]
        sizes = np.abs(weights) * exog[kept].abs().max().to_numpy(dtype=float)
        floor = 1e-07 * (float(np.abs(target).max()) or 1.0)
        involved = [c for c, size in zip(kept, sizes) if size > floor]
        if any(c in core.columns for c in involved):
            tangled += [c for c in involved if c not in protected]
    tangled = list(dict.fromkeys(tangled))
    exog = exog.drop(columns=aliased + tangled)
    note = 'aliased covariates dropped: ' + ', '.join(aliased) if aliased else ''
    note += '; covariates that rebuild the exposure with them dropped: ' + ', '.join(tangled) if tangled else ''
    endog = data[outcome_column].astype(float)
    groups = pd.factorize(data['country'])[0]
    model = sm.OLS(endog, exog)
    fit = model.fit(cov_type="cluster", cov_kwds={"groups": groups})
    note += ('; ' if note else '') + 'outcome z-scored with the predictors: ' + outcome_column
    term = 'exposure_by_moderator'
    ci = fit.conf_int()
    low, high = (float(v) for v in ci.loc[term])
    value = float(fit.params[term])
    p_value = float(fit.pvalues[term])
    return {
        "estimate": value,
        "ci_low": low,
        "ci_high": high,
        "p_value": p_value,
        "n": int(len(data)),
        "note": note,
    }

def apply(df, ctx):
    rel_cols = ["rel_1", "rel_2", "rel_3", "rel_4", "rel_5", "rel_6", "rel_7", "rel_8", "rel_9"]

def apply(df, ctx):
    c1 = df['cnorm_1'].copy()
    c2 = df['cnorm_2'].copy()
    m1, s1 = c1.mean(), c1.std()
    m2, s2 = c2.mean(), c2.std()
    z1 = (c1 - m1) / s1
    z2 = (c2 - m2) / s2
    cov_mat = np.cov(np.column_stack([z1.values, z2.values]))
    eigvals, eigvecs = np.linalg.eigh(cov_mat)
    idx = np.argmax(eigvals)
    vec = eigvecs[:, idx]
    pc1 = z1 * vec[0] + z2 * vec[1]
    items_mean = (c1 + c2) / 2
    corr = np.corrcoef(pc1, items_mean)[0, 1]
    if corr < 0:
        pc1 = -pc1
    df_out = df.copy()
    df_out['cnorm'] = pc1.values
    return df_out

def apply(df, ctx):
    c1 = df['cnorm_1'].copy()

    m1, s1 = c1.mean(), c1.std()
    m2, s2 = c2.mean(), c2.std()

    z2 = (c2 - m2) / s2

    corr = np.corrcoef(pc1, items_mean)[0, 1]

    return df

    note += ('; ' if note else '') + 'outcome z-scored with the predictors: ' + outcome_column
    term = 'exposure_by_moderator'
    ci = fit.conf_int()
    low, high = (float(v) for v in ci.loc[term])
    value = float(fit.params[term])
    p_value = float(fit.pvalues[term])
    return {
        "estimate": value,
        "ci_low": low,
        "ci_high": high,
        "p_value": p_value,
        "n": int(len(data)),
        "note": note,
    }

report.narrative: The original analysis estimated 0.0352 (95% CI 0.0182 to 0.0521, p < 0.001, n = 10,503) and returned the verdict DEPENDS ON NORMS. No combination of defensible analytical choices reversed that verdict; the minimal flip was not found. Across 29 completed universes, every one agreed with the original verdict, giving a robustness of 100%. The estimates ranged from 0.0343 to 0.0483, with the largest shifts coming from changing the well-being outcome to social well-being (0.0464) or psychological well-being (0.0434). Adding country GDP as a covariate moved the estimate to 0.0373, while using a PCA-based religiosity scale shifted it to 0.0357. Switching to OLS with country-clustered standard errors widened confidence intervals but left all verdicts unchanged. Six universes that attempted a PCA-based cultural-norms scale failed and are excluded from the robustness figure. The judge accepted the alternative well-being outcomes, the PCA religiosity scale, the extended covariate set, and the attention-check exclusion as defensible; it rejected a no-covariates option as insufficiently defensible. The PCA cultural-norms alternative was deemed defensible in principle but could not be tested because every universe containing it failed. Robustness: 100% of the analysis grid agrees with the original verdict and 0% reverses it.
caveats: The option 'OLS clustered by country' of the step 'Estimate interaction model' failed its smoke run and is not in the analysis (KeyError: ['gender_z'] | columns available (43): ['country', 'rel_1', 'rel_2', 'rel_3', 'rel_4', 'rel_5', 'rel_6', 'rel_7', 'rel_8', 'rel_9', 'cnorm_1', 'cnorm_).
6 universes could not run and are left out of the robustness figure: failed 6 in 'PCA first component' (the process was stopped, exit code -1).

In 16 universes the model z-scores the outcome 'wb_overall_mean', 'wb_psych_mean', 'wb_soc_mean' as well as the predictors, because the decision rule reads a standardised coefficient: those estimates are in standard deviations of the outcome per standard deviation of the exposure, even where an option's description names the raw outcome.
The decision 'Create cultural norms scale' was not tested: every universe with one of its alternatives ('PCA first component') failed, so the robustness figure says nothing about it.

Robustness headline: 100% of the analysis grid agrees with the original verdict (uniform random sample of the grid: 12 draws (each decision picks each of its options equally), 6 distinct results; independent of the beam search). Among the universes the search explored, 100% agree, but the beam search samples the universes that are closest to flipping, so that share leans toward flips.
